free.title: Free Kayaking at Pier 26
free.caption:
OUTDOORS · TRIBECA

Free kayaking on the Hudson River is still on, and the season clock is ticking.

The Downtown Boathouse has been putting New Yorkers on the water at Pier 26 in Hudson River Park for free since the 90s. Every Saturday and Sunday through October 4 you can walk up, sign a waiver, grab a kayak and paddle the calm embayment with One WTC over your shoulder. No reservation, no gear, no charge. Weeknight sessions wrapped on Aug 27, so weekends are the only way in now.

Tip: the signup line can close early on busy days, so land before noon and wear things that can get splashed.

Send this to the friend who swears summer is not over yet.

food.title: Time Out Market New York
food.caption:
FOOD · DUMBO

Time Out Market New York is the cheat code for a Brooklyn food crawl in one building.

Inside 55 Water St in DUMBO you get Ess-a-Bagel, Jacob's Pickles, Clinton St. Baking Company, Bark Barbecue and Mori Mori by Masaharu Morimoto, plus three bars, all under one roof and open until 11PM on Saturdays. Entry is free - you only pay for what you eat.

The real move: carry your haul up to the fifth-floor rooftop, where the Brooklyn Bridge and Manhattan skyline view costs exactly nothing.

Tag the friend who can never pick one restaurant.

art.title: SUMMIT One Vanderbilt
art.caption:
ART · MIDTOWN

SUMMIT One Vanderbilt is what happens when an observation deck becomes an immersive art piece.

Three floors of mirrored rooms by Kenzo Digital multiply the Manhattan skyline into infinity, and the Levitation glass skyboxes hang 1,100 feet above Madison Avenue. It runs daily from 8AM to midnight with last entry at 10:30PM, and the entrance hides inside Grand Central's main concourse. Tickets start at $39 plus a $3 online fee.

Locals' angle: book the sunset slot a few days out, then stay after dark when the mirror rooms flip to city-lights mode.
